title: Turkish Eggs
subtitle: Cilbir: poached eggs on garlicky yoghurt with chilli butter
excerpt: Turkish eggs, known as cilbir, are poached eggs served on a bed of cold garlicky yoghurt with a hot butter and paprika drizzle poured over at the table. The contrast of temperatures makes this dish. It takes about 20 minutes from start to finish.
sourceNotes: Cilbir has been eaten in Turkey since at least the 15th century. It was historically a dish served to Ottoman sultans and remains a popular Turkish breakfast today.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The garlic yoghurt can be made up to 24 hours ahead and kept refrigerated.

content.text: The yoghurt should be cold and the butter drizzle should be very hot when they meet on the plate. Pour the butter on just before serving so it sizzles when it hits the cold yoghurt.

items.prepNote: at room temperature is fine; serve cold

content.text: Mix the yoghurt with the garlic and lemon juice. Season with salt. Spread across 4 plates.
Fill the large saucepan with water to a depth of about 6 cm. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Crack one egg into a small cup. Stir the water to create a swirl, then slide the egg in. Poach 2 to 3 eggs at a time.
Cook for 3 minutes for a runny yolk. Lift out with a slotted spoon.
Place 2 eggs on top of the yoghurt on each plate.
Melt the butter in the small frying pan over a medium-high heat until it begins to foam.
Add the paprika and chilli flakes. Stir for 10 seconds. The butter should be very hot.
Spoon the hot chilli butter over the eggs immediately.
Scatter dill over the top and serve straight away.

items.symptom: The butter turns dark brown before the spices go in.
items.cause: Heat was too high and butter burned.
items.fix: Wipe pan and start again on medium heat only.

items.symptom: The yoghurt is watery and pools on the plate.
items.cause: Greek yoghurt has higher water content or was stirred too vigorously.
items.fix: Drain yoghurt through a sieve for 10 minutes before using.
